question: In 1851, who founded the science of hydrodynamics with his law of viscosity describing the velocity of a small sphere through a viscous fluid?
solution_text:
The correct answer is George Gabriel Stokes.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sir George Gabriel Stokes (1819-1903), an Irish-British mathematician and physicist, formulated Stokes' Law in 1851, describing the drag force (viscosity-related resistance) on a small sphere moving through a viscous fluid. (श्यानता का नियम — जॉर्ज गेब्रियल स्टोक्स)

 

• Stokes' Law is expressed as F = 6πηrv, where η is the coefficient of viscosity, r is the radius of the sphere, and v is its velocity — it laid the mathematical foundation for the science of hydrodynamics.

 

• Stokes also contributed significantly to the wave theory of light, fluorescence, and the Navier-Stokes equations, which describe the motion of viscous fluid substances.

 

• He served as the Lucasian Professor of Mathematics at the University of Cambridge, the same chair once held by Isaac Newton.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Navier-Stokes equations, jointly attributed to Claude-Louis Navier and George Gabriel Stokes, remain fundamental to fluid mechanics, weather modelling, and aerodynamics.

 

• Stokes' Law is widely used to determine the terminal velocity of particles settling in a viscous medium, such as in Millikan's oil-drop experiment.

 

NOTE

 

• Daniel Bernoulli (Option 1): Known for Bernoulli's principle, relating fluid pressure and velocity, published in his 1738 work *Hydrodynamica*.

 

• Evangelista Torricelli (Option 3): Known for inventing the barometer and for Torricelli's Law of fluid efflux, not the viscosity law.

 

• Heinrich Gustav Magnus (Option 4): Known for discovering the Magnus effect, describing the force on a spinning object moving through a fluid.

question: The rate at which the Reserve Bank of India lends to other commercial banks for short term has been reduced. What is this rate called?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Repo Rate.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Repo Rate (Repurchase Rate) is the interest rate at which the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) lends short-term funds to commercial banks against government securities. (रेपो दर — अल्पकालिक ऋण दर)

 

• A reduction in the repo rate makes borrowing cheaper for commercial banks, which in turn can lower interest rates for consumers, encouraging investment and spending in the economy.

 

• Repo Rate is one of the key tools used by the RBI's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) to control inflation and manage liquidity in the banking system.

 

• It is currently determined and reviewed periodically by the RBI's Monetary Policy Committee, headed by the RBI Governor.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Reverse Repo Rate is the rate at which the RBI borrows money from commercial banks, the opposite of the repo rate mechanism.

 

• The Bank Rate is the rate at which RBI lends long-term funds to banks without any collateral security, unlike the repo rate which requires collateral.

 

NOTE

 

• Cash Reserve Rate (Option 1): Refers to the Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR), the minimum percentage of a bank's deposits that must be kept with the RBI, not a lending rate.

 

• Reverse Repo Rate (Option 2): The rate at which RBI borrows from banks, not lends to them.

 

• Bank Rate (Option 3): A long-term, collateral-free lending rate, distinct from the short-term, collateralised repo rate described in the question.

question: What was the percentage of India's population that belonged to the Muslim religion in 2011?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 14.2%.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the 2011 Census of India, Muslims constituted 14.2% of India's total population, making them the second-largest religious group after Hindus. (2011 जनगणना — मुस्लिम जनसंख्या 14.2%)

 

• The 2011 Census recorded Hindus at 79.8%, Muslims at 14.2%, Christians at 2.3%, Sikhs at 1.7%, Buddhists at 0.7%, and Jains at 0.4% of the total population.

 

• The 2011 Census was the 15th National Census of India, conducted in two phases — house-listing and population enumeration.

 

• The census recorded India's total population as approximately 121 crore (1.21 billion).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 2011 Census was conducted under the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India, and its motto was "Our Census, Our future".

 

• The next decadal census (originally due 2021) has been delayed and is now expected to be conducted in the coming years.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 2, 3 and 4 (11.9%, 16.4%, 18.5%) are all incorrect figures that do not match the actual 2011 Census religious composition data for the Muslim population.

question: Kerala is famous for which of the following festivals?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Onam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Onam is the most important and famous harvest festival of Kerala, celebrated annually in the Malayalam month of Chingam (August-September). (ओणम — केरल का प्रमुख त्योहार)

 

• It commemorates the homecoming of the mythical King Mahabali, and is marked by the Pookalam (floral rangoli), Onasadya (grand feast), Vallam Kali (snake boat races) and Kathakali performances.

 

• Onam is celebrated over ten days, with the tenth day, Thiru Onam, being the most significant.

 

• It is a state festival of Kerala, celebrated by people of all religions and communities within the state.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The famous Nehru Trophy Boat Race, a snake boat race, is held on the Pamba River at Alappuzha as part of Onam-season celebrations.

 

• Kerala's other notable festivals include Vishu (Malayalam New Year) and Thrissur Pooram.

 

NOTE

 

• Pongal (Option 1): A harvest festival celebrated in Tamil Nadu.

 

• Ugadi (Option 2): The New Year festival celebrated in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Karnataka.

 

• Bihu (Option 3): The harvest/New Year festival celebrated in Assam.

question: Guru Gopinath National Award 2021 was honoured to whom among the following Kathak dancers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kumudini Lakhia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kumudini Lakhia (1930-2020s), a legendary exponent and choreographer of Kathak, was honoured with the Guru Gopinath National Award 2021 (posthumously) for her outstanding contribution to the dance form. (कुमुदिनी लाखिया — कथक नृत्यांगना)

 

• She was the founder of the Kadamb Centre for Dance, Music and Related Arts in Ahmedabad and is credited with modernising Kathak choreography by introducing group compositions and contemporary themes.

 

• Among her honours were the Padma Shri (1987) and Padma Bhushan (2010) from the Government of India.

 

• The Guru Gopinath National Award is instituted in memory of Guru Gopinath, a pioneering figure of Kerala's classical dance tradition, and is given to eminent classical dancers across styles.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kumudini Lakhia trained under Sanyukta Panigrahi and other stalwarts before establishing her own distinct style within traditional Kathak.

 

• Kathak is one of the eight classical dance forms of India, with major gharanas in Lucknow, Jaipur and Banaras.

 

NOTE

 

• Durga Lal (Option 1): A noted Kathak exponent of the Jaipur gharana, awarded the Padma Shri, but not the recipient referenced here.

 

• Roshan Kumari (Option 2): A well-known Kathak dancer of the Jaipur gharana, but not the awardee in this instance.

 

• Shambhu Maharaj (Option 4): A celebrated Kathak guru of the Lucknow gharana, but not the recipient of this particular award.

question: Which of these statements is true?
option_1: Under competitive asset market conditions, the price of a bond must always be equal to its present value in equilibrium.
option_2: Under competitive asset market conditions, the price of a bond must be less than its present value to benefit the seller.
option_3: Under competitive asset market conditions, the price of a bond must exceed its present value to benefit the buyer.
option_4: Under competitive asset market conditions, the present value must exceed the price of a bond to benefit the seller.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Under competitive asset market conditions, the price of a bond must always be equal to its present value in equilibrium.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In competitive (efficient) asset markets, the price of a financial asset (such as a bond) equals its present value (PV) in equilibrium, since all available information is reflected in the price. (बाण्ड की कीमत — वर्तमान मूल्य के बराबर)

 

• Present Value (PV) is the current worth of a stream of future cash flows (coupon payments and face value) discounted at an appropriate interest rate.

 

• If the price were below present value, buyers would rush to purchase the bond (as it is undervalued), pushing the price up until it equals PV; if the price were above PV, sellers would rush to sell, pushing the price down — this arbitrage-driven adjustment ensures price = PV at equilibrium.

 

• This is a foundational concept in monetary economics and the theory of asset pricing, as discussed in standard texts on money, banking and financial markets.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• This principle underlies the efficient markets hypothesis, which states that asset prices fully reflect all available information at any given time.

 

• Bond prices and interest rates move inversely — as market interest rates rise, the present value (and hence price) of existing bonds falls, and vice versa.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2: Incorrect — a price below present value benefits the buyer, not the seller, since the buyer is acquiring an undervalued asset.

 

• Option 3: Incorrect — a price above present value benefits the seller, not the buyer, since the buyer would be overpaying.

 

• Option 4: Incorrect — if present value exceeds price, it benefits the buyer (who gets the asset cheap), not the seller.

question: Which of these is NOT one of the negative effects of the green revolution?
option_1: Primarily medium and large farmers were able to benefit from the new technology of the green revolution.
option_2: The green revolution benefited farmers who had access to land, capital, technology and know-how.
option_3: The green revolution led to the displacement of tenant cultivators in many cases.
option_4: The green revolution caused increased migration from urban to rural areas.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The green revolution caused increased migration from urban to rural areas.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Green Revolution (from the mid-1960s) actually intensified rural-to-urban migration, not urban-to-rural migration, as mechanisation reduced the demand for agricultural labour and displaced small and marginal farmers/tenants who then moved to cities in search of work. (हरित क्रांति — ग्रामीण से शहरी पलायन)

 

• Statement 4 reverses the actual, well-documented direction of migration, which is why it is NOT a genuine (or even accurate) negative effect of the Green Revolution.

 

• Genuine negative effects included increased regional and interpersonal income inequality, since medium and large farmers with access to capital, irrigation and inputs benefited disproportionately over small and marginal farmers.

 

• The Green Revolution also led to displacement of tenant cultivators, as landowners resumed personal cultivation to capture the higher profits made possible by the new technology.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other criticisms of the Green Revolution include excessive use of chemical fertilisers and pesticides, groundwater depletion, and its concentrated focus on wheat and rice in states like Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh.

 

• The Green Revolution in India was spearheaded by agricultural scientist M.S. Swaminathan, often called the "Father of the Green Revolution in India".

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1: This is a genuine, well-documented negative effect — medium and large farmers benefited disproportionately, so it is correctly identified as a negative effect (and hence not the answer to this "NOT" question).

 

• Option 2: Similarly a genuine negative effect — farmers with access to land, capital, technology and know-how gained the most, worsening inequality.

 

• Option 3: A genuine negative effect — tenant cultivators were frequently displaced as landowners took back land for self-cultivation.

question:
Which of the following is included in the M1 measure of money supply?

A) Currency with Public

B) Time Deposit with Post Office

C) Demand Deposits with Commercial Banks/RBI of Public Financial Institutions
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both A and C.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• M1, the narrowest measure of money supply defined by the RBI, comprises Currency with the Public + Demand Deposits with Banks + Other Deposits with the RBI. (मुद्रा आपूर्ति — M1 माप)

 

• M1 = Currency with Public (A) + Demand Deposits with Commercial Banks/RBI (C) + Other Deposits with RBI, making both statements A and C correct components of M1.

 

• Time deposits (statement B), such as fixed/term deposits with banks or the post office, are not part of M1 because they are not immediately liquid/spendable — they are included only in broader aggregates like M2 and M3.

 

• The RBI classifies money supply into four measures: M1, M2, M3 and M4, in decreasing order of liquidity.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• M3 (broad money) = M1 + Time Deposits with banks, and is the most widely used measure for monetary policy analysis in India.

 

• M4 = M3 + all deposits with the Post Office Savings Banks (excluding National Savings Certificates), making it the broadest and least liquid measure.

 

NOTE

 

• Both B and C (Option 1): Incorrect, as it wrongly includes Time Deposit with Post Office (B), which is not part of M1.

 

• Only B (Option 3): Incorrect, since Time Deposits are excluded from M1 altogether.

 

• Only A (Option 4): Incomplete, as it omits Demand Deposits (C), which is also a valid component of M1.

question: Indian Academy of Sciences, founded in 1934 by CV Raman, is situated in ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bangalore.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indian Academy of Sciences (IASc) was founded in 1934 by the Nobel laureate physicist Sir C.V. Raman, and is headquartered in Bangalore (Bengaluru), Karnataka. (भारतीय विज्ञान अकादमी — बेंगलुरु)

 

• It is one of India's premier science academies, promoting the progress and dissemination of scientific knowledge, and publishes several peer-reviewed journals such as *Current Science*.

 

• C.V. Raman served as its first President and was also the founder of the Raman Research Institute, also located in Bangalore.

 

• The Academy elects Fellows from across scientific disciplines based on outstanding contributions to science.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• C.V. Raman won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1930 for the discovery of the Raman Effect, related to the scattering of light.

 

• India's other major science academies include the National Academy of Sciences, India (NASI) in Prayagraj (Allahabad) and the Indian National Science Academy (INSA) in New Delhi.

 

NOTE

 

• Mumbai (Option 1), Hyderabad (Option 2) and New Delhi (Option 4) are all incorrect — the Indian Academy of Sciences has always been headquartered in Bangalore since its founding.

question: Who amongst the following raised the banner of revolt against Nasiruddin Khusrau?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ghazi Malik, later known as Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq, raised the banner of revolt against Khusrau Khan (Nasiruddin Khusrau Shah), defeated and killed him in 1320, and founded the Tughlaq dynasty. (गयासुद्दीन तुगलक — तुगलक वंश के संस्थापक)

 

• Khusrau Khan had usurped the throne of Delhi after murdering the last ruler of the Khilji dynasty, Sultan Qutbuddin Mubarak Shah Khilji, in 1320.

 

• Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq, then governor of Dipalpur, marched on Delhi, defeated Khusrau Khan, and ascended the throne as the first Sultan of the Tughlaq dynasty (1320-1414).

 

• He built the fortified city of Tughlaqabad near Delhi and ruled until 1325.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq died in 1325 in a controversial incident involving the collapse of a wooden pavilion, allegedly engineered by his son Muhammad bin Tughlaq, who succeeded him.

 

• The Tughlaq dynasty was the longest-ruling dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate.

 

NOTE

 

• Nasiruddin Tughlaq (Option 1): A later, weak ruler of the Tughlaq dynasty (r. 1394-1395), unrelated to the revolt against Khusrau Khan.

 

• Muhammad bin Tughlaq (Option 2): Son and successor of Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq, known for his ambitious but often disastrous administrative experiments, not the one who revolted against Khusrau Khan.

 

• Feroz Shah Tughlaq (Option 3): A later Tughlaq ruler (r. 1351-1388), known for public works and welfare measures, not connected to the revolt against Khusrau Khan.

question: When milk is converted into curd, which type of change is it?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chemical change.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The conversion of milk into curd is a chemical change, brought about by the fermentation action of lactic acid bacteria (Lactobacillus), which convert lactose (milk sugar) into lactic acid. (दूध से दही — रासायनिक परिवर्तन)

 

• The lactic acid produced causes the milk proteins (casein) to denature and coagulate, forming a new substance (curd) with different chemical composition and properties from milk.

 

• Since a new substance is formed and the change cannot be reversed back into milk by simple physical means, it qualifies as a chemical change, not a physical or reversible one.

 

• This process is a form of fermentation, a biochemical reaction commonly used in food preservation and processing.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other examples of chemical changes include burning of fuel, rusting of iron, and cooking of food.

 

• Examples of physical changes (no new substance formed, generally reversible) include melting of ice, evaporation of water, and dissolving sugar in water.

 

NOTE

 

• Reversible change (Option 1): Incorrect, as curd cannot be converted back into milk — the transformation is irreversible.

 

• Physical change (Option 2): Incorrect, as a physical change does not involve formation of a new substance, whereas curd is chemically distinct from milk.

 

• Isothermal change (Option 3): Incorrect; an isothermal change refers to a thermodynamic process occurring at constant temperature, which is not the defining characteristic of milk turning to curd.

question: Which of the following persons' tenure was extended for one year as Chief of the Enforcement Directorate in November 2021 ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sanjay Kumar Mishra.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sanjay Kumar Mishra, who took over as Director of the Enforcement Directorate (ED) in November 2018, had his tenure extended by one year in November 2021 through an ordinance amending the Central Vigilance Commission Act. (संजय कुमार मिश्रा — प्रवर्तन निदेशालय)

 

• The Enforcement Directorate (ED) is a law enforcement and economic intelligence agency under the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, responsible for enforcing laws like the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) and FEMA.

 

• Mishra's tenure was subsequently extended multiple times through government orders and legal proceedings, drawing significant political and judicial attention.

 

• The Supreme Court of India later scrutinised these extensions, ultimately directing that his tenure not be extended further beyond July 2023.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Enforcement Directorate is headquartered in New Delhi and has zonal offices across major Indian cities.

 

• The ED works closely with agencies like the CBI and Income Tax Department in investigating financial crimes.

 

NOTE

 

• Pradyumna Sinha, Prateek Rai and Vijay Verma (Options 1, 3, 4): None of these individuals held the position of, or had their tenure extended as, Director of the Enforcement Directorate in November 2021; that distinction belongs to Sanjay Kumar Mishra.

question: Which of the following physical divisions of India is densely populated?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The North Indian Plains.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The North Indian Plains (Indo-Gangetic Plains), formed by the alluvial deposits of the Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra river systems, are the most densely populated physical division of India due to their extremely fertile soil, flat terrain, and abundant water supply. (उत्तर भारतीय मैदान — सर्वाधिक घनी आबादी)

 

• These plains support intensive agriculture, particularly of rice and wheat, and host some of India's largest cities and states, including Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal and Punjab.

 

• In contrast, regions like the Himalayas, deserts and islands have rugged terrain, extreme climate, or poor soil, limiting habitability and agricultural productivity.

 

• The Indo-Gangetic Plains stretch nearly 3,200 km from the Indus valley in the west to the Brahmaputra valley in the east.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The North Indian Plains are divided into the Bhabar, Terai, Bhangar and Khadar regions based on soil and terrain characteristics.

 

• Uttar Pradesh, located in the Indo-Gangetic Plains, is the most populous state in India.

 

NOTE

 

• The islands (Option 2): Sparsely populated due to isolation and limited land area, e.g., Andaman & Nicobar and Lakshadweep.

 

• The Himalayan Range (Option 3): Sparsely populated due to high altitude, rugged terrain and harsh climate.

 

• The Thar Desert (Option 4): Sparsely populated due to arid conditions and scarcity of water.

question: Which of the following is a liberal principle of the Directive Principles of State Policy of the Indian Constitution ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is To secure uniform civil code.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP), based on their content and philosophy, are classified into three broad categories: Gandhian, Socialist, and Liberal-Intellectual principles. (नीति निदेशक तत्व — उदार सिद्धांत)

 

• The Uniform Civil Code (Article 44), which directs the State to secure a common civil code for all citizens, is classified as a Liberal-Intellectual principle, reflecting the ideals of modern liberal democracy.

 

• Other Liberal-Intellectual principles include organising village panchayats (Article 40), separation of judiciary from the executive (Article 50), and promoting international peace and security (Article 51).

 

• These principles reflect the ideology of liberalism, focused on individual rights, rational governance and modern institutional reform, distinct from Gandhian (village-based) or Socialist (welfare-based) principles.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• DPSPs are enshrined in Part IV (Articles 36-51) of the Indian Constitution and are non-justiciable but fundamental in the governance of the country.

 

• The concept of DPSPs was borrowed from the Irish Constitution, which in turn borrowed it from the Spanish Constitution.

 

NOTE

 

• To secure right to work (Option 1): Classified as a Socialist principle (Article 41), aimed at economic and social justice.

 

• To promote social welfare (Option 3): Also a Socialist principle, reflecting the welfare-state orientation of several DPSPs.

 

• To promote equal justice (Option 4): Free legal aid and equal justice (Article 39A) is generally classed alongside socialist/welfare-oriented objectives, not the liberal-intellectual category.

question: Gurucharan Singh received the Padma Shri from the Government of India in 2023 for his contributions to the sport of ____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is cricket.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gurcharan Singh, a veteran cricket coach and former head coach of the Indian women's cricket team, was honoured with the Padma Shri in 2023 for his contribution to the sport of cricket. (गुरचरण सिंह — क्रिकेट कोच)

 

• He was conferred the award alongside other sports personalities on Republic Day 2023, recognising decades of contribution to coaching and nurturing Indian cricketing talent.

 

• Gurcharan Singh has been associated with coaching at various levels, including with the BCCI and state cricket associations.

 

• The Padma Shri is the fourth-highest civilian award in the Republic of India, awarded for distinguished contributions in various fields including sports.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other sportspersons honoured with the Padma Shri in 2023 included Sanathoiba Sharma (wushu coach) and Deepika Kumari (archery).

 

• The Padma Awards are announced annually on the eve of Republic Day (26 January).

 

NOTE

 

• Football, basketball and kabaddi (Options 1, 2, 3): These are not the sport associated with Gurcharan Singh's 2023 Padma Shri; his recognised contribution was in cricket coaching.

question: Which of the following is NOT a capital expenditure for the central government?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Salaries and old-age pensions.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Salaries and old-age pensions are recurring, consumption-type payments that do not create or add to any asset of the government, and are therefore classified as revenue expenditure, not capital expenditure. (राजस्व व्यय — वेतन और पेंशन)

 

• Capital expenditure refers to spending that either creates an asset (like infrastructure) or reduces a liability, and includes items like loans to state governments, acquisition/improvement of fixed assets, and construction of roads and bridges.

 

• Loans to state governments (Option 1), improvement of fixed assets (Option 2), and construction of roads and bridges (Option 4) all result in asset creation or represent investment, and are hence capital expenditure.

 

• The Union Budget of India classifies total expenditure into Revenue Expenditure and Capital Expenditure, as per Article 112 of the Constitution.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other examples of revenue expenditure include interest payments, subsidies, and grants-in-aid, none of which create durable assets.

 

• A rising share of capital expenditure in the budget is generally seen as positive for long-term economic growth, as it builds productive infrastructure.

 

NOTE

 

• Loan to state government (Option 1): A capital expenditure, as it represents an asset (a receivable) for the central government.

 

• Improvement of fixed assets (Option 2): A capital expenditure, as it enhances the value/life of existing government assets.

 

• Construction of roads and bridges (Option 4): A capital expenditure, as it creates new physical infrastructure assets.

question: Which of the following is a yellowish green to green coloured gemstone often found in mafic and ultramafic igneous rocks such as basalt, gabbro, dunite, diabase and peridotite?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Olivine.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Olivine is a yellowish-green to green coloured silicate mineral/gemstone, commonly found in mafic and ultramafic igneous rocks such as basalt, gabbro, dunite, diabase and peridotite. (ओलिवीन — हरे रंग का रत्न)

 

• Its gem-quality variety is known as peridot, widely used in jewellery and prized for its distinctive olive-green colour, caused by traces of iron in its crystal structure.

 

• Olivine is a magnesium iron silicate, chemically represented as (Mg,Fe)₂SiO₄, and is one of the most abundant minerals in the Earth's upper mantle.

 

• It typically crystallises early from magma at high temperatures, making it common in dark-coloured, iron- and magnesium-rich (mafic/ultramafic) rocks.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Peridot, the gem form of olivine, is the birthstone for the month of August.

 

• Olivine-rich rocks are also studied for their potential in carbon capture, since olivine reacts with CO₂ to form stable carbonate minerals.

 

NOTE

 

• Bornite (Option 1): A copper iron sulfide mineral known as "peacock ore" for its iridescent purplish tarnish, not a green gemstone.

 

• Tremolite (Option 3): A calcium magnesium silicate mineral of the amphibole group, typically white to grey or pale green, and not specifically associated with mafic/ultramafic rocks in the way olivine is.

 

• Garnet (Option 4): A group of silicate minerals typically red, brown or (rarely) green in colour, found in metamorphic rocks, not primarily in mafic/ultramafic igneous rocks.

question: Which of the following is a public sector industry?
solution_text:
The correct answer is BHEL.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• BHEL (Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited), established in 1964, is a Maharatna Public Sector Undertaking (PSU) under the Ministry of Heavy Industries, Government of India. (भेल — सार्वजनिक क्षेत्र उपक्रम)

 

• BHEL is India's largest engineering and manufacturing company in the energy-related and infrastructure sector, producing power plant equipment, turbines, and industrial machinery.

 

• It is headquartered in New Delhi and has multiple manufacturing units across India, including at Bhopal, Haridwar, Hyderabad and Tiruchirappalli.

 

• Being a public sector enterprise, the majority ownership and control of BHEL rests with the Government of India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• BHEL was among the first Indian PSUs to be granted Maharatna status (in 2013), granting it greater financial and operational autonomy.

 

• Other major PSUs in the heavy engineering sector include SAIL (Steel Authority of India Limited) and NTPC.

 

NOTE

 

• Dabur Industry (Option 2): A private sector company, one of India's leading FMCG and ayurvedic products manufacturers.

 

• Bajaj Auto (Option 3): A private sector company, a leading two-wheeler and three-wheeler manufacturer, part of the Bajaj Group.

 

• TISCO (Option 4): Tata Iron and Steel Company (now Tata Steel) is a private sector company under the Tata Group, not government-owned.

question: Who was the author of the famous book 'The Economic History of India'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is RC Dutt.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Romesh Chunder Dutt (R.C. Dutt), an eminent Indian civil servant, economic historian and nationalist, authored the seminal two-volume work 'The Economic History of India' (published in 1902 and 1904). (आर.सी. दत्त — भारत का आर्थिक इतिहास)

 

• The book is a landmark critique of British colonial economic policies, arguing that they led to the "drain of wealth" from India and the systematic impoverishment of Indian agriculture and industry.

 

• R.C. Dutt was among the first Indians to qualify for the Indian Civil Service (ICS) and later served as President of the Indian National Congress in 1899.

 

• His economic writings significantly influenced the nationalist "Drain of Wealth" theory, alongside the works of Dadabhai Naoroji.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• R.C. Dutt also translated the Ramayana and Mahabharata into English verse and wrote extensively on Indian history and society.

 

• The "Drain of Wealth" theory, articulating how British policies extracted India's wealth to Britain, was most famously propounded by Dadabhai Naoroji in his book *Poverty and Un-British Rule in India*.

 

NOTE

 

• Dadabhai Naoroji (Option 1): Known for the "Drain of Wealth" theory and his book *Poverty and Un-British Rule in India*, not the author of 'The Economic History of India'.

 

• PC Dutta (Option 2): Not a recognised author of this particular work.

 

• RG Bhandarkar (Option 3): A noted Sanskrit scholar and Indologist, not associated with authoring this economic history text.

question: Jagoi and Thabal Chongba are the famous dances of which Indian state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Manipur.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Jagoi and Thabal Chongba are traditional folk/classical dance forms of Manipur, deeply rooted in the state's cultural and religious life. (जागोई और थबल चोंगबा — मणिपुर के लोकनृत्य)

 

• Jagoi refers to the classical dance style associated with Manipuri Ras Lila, characterised by graceful, fluid movements depicting themes from Vaishnavite tradition (Radha-Krishna).

 

• Thabal Chongba is a traditional group folk dance performed under moonlight, typically during the Yaoshang (Holi) festival, where men and women dance together in a circle.

 

• Manipuri dance is one of the eight classical dance forms of India, known for its devotional themes and gentle, flowing movements.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important dance forms of Manipur include the Pung Cholom (drum dance) and Lai Haraoba, a ritual dance dedicated to local deities.

 

• Manipur's capital is Imphal, and the state is also known for Sangai (the dancing deer) and Loktak Lake.

 

NOTE

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 1): Known for dance forms like Kathak and Raslila (different regional traditions), not Jagoi/Thabal Chongba.

 

• Odisha (Option 2): Known for Odissi classical dance, not Jagoi/Thabal Chongba.

 

• Nagaland (Option 4): Known for various tribal war dances and the Hornbill Festival, not Jagoi/Thabal Chongba.

question: In 2023, which Indian Tennis player became the oldest to win the ATP Masters 1000 title?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rohan Bopanna.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rohan Bopanna, partnering with Australia's Matthew Ebden, won the men's doubles title at the 2023 BNP Paribas Open (Indian Wells Masters), becoming the oldest player to win an ATP Masters 1000 title at the age of 42. (रोहन बोपन्ना — सबसे उम्रदराज एटीपी मास्टर्स 1000 विजेता)

 

• The pair defeated Rajeev Ram and Joe Salisbury in the final, with media widely covering Bopanna's remarkable achievement as "coffee-powered" longevity in professional tennis at Indian Wells in March 2023.

 

• The ATP Masters 1000 series comprises the nine most prestigious tournaments on the ATP Tour below the Grand Slams.

 

• Bopanna went on to further doubles success, including winning the 2024 Australian Open men's doubles title, becoming the oldest world No. 1 in doubles history.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rohan Bopanna has also won multiple Grand Slam mixed doubles titles, including the 2017 French Open (with Gabriela Dabrowski).

 

• He represented India in four Olympic Games and has been a mainstay of Indian doubles tennis for over two decades.

 

NOTE

 

• Mahesh Bhupathi (Option 2): A legendary Indian doubles player of an earlier generation, not associated with this 2023 record.

 

• Vijay Amritraj (Option 3): A former Indian tennis star of the 1970s-80s, not connected to this achievement.

 

• Ramanathan Krishnan (Option 4): A pioneering Indian tennis player of the 1950s-60s, unrelated to this modern-day record.

question: In 1830, which American scientist created the world's most powerful electromagnet, the Albany magnet, which could lift up to 750 pounds of metal at a time?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Joseph Henry.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Joseph Henry, an American scientist, built the world's most powerful electromagnet of its time in 1830-31 while working at the Albany Academy in New York, capable of lifting several hundred pounds of iron. (जोसेफ हेनरी — शक्तिशाली विद्युत चुंबक)

 

• This device, often referred to as the "Albany magnet", demonstrated remarkable lifting capacity for its era and advanced the practical understanding of electromagnetism.

 

• Henry is also credited with discovering the electromagnetic phenomenon of self-inductance, and the SI unit of inductance, the henry (H), is named after him.

 

• He later became the first Secretary of the Smithsonian Institution in Washington, D.C.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Joseph Henry's work on electromagnets and induction laid crucial groundwork later built upon by Michael Faraday and others in the development of electric motors and generators.

 

• He also contributed significantly to early telegraph technology, having built a working electric telegraph system before Samuel Morse's commercial version.

 

NOTE

 

• John Cockcroft (Option 1): A 20th-century British physicist known for splitting the atomic nucleus (Cockcroft-Walton experiment), unrelated to the Albany magnet.

 

• William Gilbert (Option 2): An English scientist from the 16th-17th century known for foundational studies on magnetism (*De Magnete*), but not the creator of the Albany magnet.

 

• Edward Purcell (Option 4): A 20th-century American physicist known for co-discovering Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR), unrelated to the 1830 Albany magnet.

question: Who was the first American male athlete to win the Marathon gold medal in the Olympic Games?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Thomas Hicks.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Thomas Hicks, an English-born American athlete, won the men's marathon gold medal at the 1904 St. Louis Olympic Games, becoming the first American male athlete to achieve this feat. (थॉमस हिक्स — पहला अमेरिकी मैराथन स्वर्ण विजेता)

 

• Hicks completed the race in a controversial manner, having been administered strychnine and brandy by his trainers during the race, a substance later banned as performance-enhancing.

 

• The 1904 Olympic marathon was infamous for its harsh conditions — extreme heat, dust from accompanying vehicles, and a lack of water stations along the course.

 

• Hicks had emigrated from England to the United States, representing the USA in this event.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• John Hayes (Option 4) later won the 1908 London Olympics marathon for the USA, following a controversial disqualification of the initial finisher, Dorando Pietri of Italy.

 

• The Olympic marathon distance was standardised at 26.2 miles (42.195 km) starting from the 1908 London Games.

 

NOTE

 

• Abebe Bikila (Option 1): An Ethiopian athlete famous for winning marathon gold at the 1960 Rome and 1964 Tokyo Olympics, running barefoot in Rome — not American.

 

• Frank Shorter (Option 3): An American athlete who won the marathon gold at the 1972 Munich Olympics, but not the first American to do so, as Thomas Hicks had already achieved this in 1904.

 

• John Hayes (Option 4): Won gold for the USA at the 1908 London Olympics, making him the second American, not the first.

question: Which of the following Articles about fundamental duties is related to the respect of the National Anthem?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 51A (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 51A(a) of the Indian Constitution, under the Fundamental Duties (Part IVA), states that it is the duty of every citizen "to abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem". (अनुच्छेद 51क(क) — राष्ट्रगान का सम्मान)

 

• The Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution via the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.

 

• Originally, 10 Fundamental Duties were incorporated; an 11th duty was later added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002, relating to providing education to children aged 6-14 years.

 

• These duties are non-justiciable, meaning they cannot be directly enforced by courts, but serve as a moral obligation on citizens.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The concept of Fundamental Duties was inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR (Soviet Union).

 

• Article 51A(g) relates to the duty to protect and improve the natural environment, another commonly tested provision.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 51A(b) (Option 1): Relates to the duty "to cherish and follow the noble ideals which inspired our national struggle for freedom".

 

• Article 51A(c) (Option 2): Relates to the duty "to uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India".

 

• Article 51A(d) (Option 4): Relates to the duty "to defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so".

question: Begum Akhtar is associated with which of the following fields?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ghazal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Begum Akhtar (1914-1974), popularly known as the "Mallika-e-Ghazal" (Queen of Ghazal), was a legendary Indian singer renowned for her rendition of Ghazals, Thumris and Dadras. (बेगम अख्तर — गजल की मल्लिका)

 

• She was honoured with the Padma Shri (1968) and posthumously the Padma Bhushan (1975) by the Government of India for her contribution to Hindustani classical and semi-classical vocal music.

 

• Her soulful renditions of Urdu poetry set to music greatly popularised the Ghazal genre among the masses in India.

 

• She trained under renowned gurus including Ustad Ata Mohammed Khan and belonged to the Patiala gharana tradition of vocal music.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• A Google Doodle was dedicated to Begum Akhtar on her birth anniversary, honouring her contribution to Indian music.

 

• Other legendary ghazal singers of India include Jagjit Singh and Mehdi Hassan (Pakistan).

 

NOTE

 

• Writing (Option 1): Not Begum Akhtar's field of recognition; she was a performing vocalist, not primarily known as a writer.

 

• Politics (Option 2): Begum Akhtar had no notable association with politics.

 

• Painting (Option 3): Not related to Begum Akhtar's field of fame, which was music/vocal performance.
